Four stages: 1) get a dry doe ready for cross (good diet ~2 months before) → 2) record the cross — she waits for the scan → 3) record the ultrasound around 45–60 days, which confirms her and sets the kids count → 4) she moves to confirmed pregnant with a due date, until she kids.

Breeding groups (buck groups)

put one buck with a set of does · every doe keeps her own record

What needs doing

Season plan

A doe gives birth once a year, so a group crossed in April gives birth in September and is crossed again the following April. Run two groups six months apart and the farm has births twice a year. The birth window is the one date you choose — the green row; everything else is counted from it.

Monthly stock check

count the store, correct the books
Once a month, weigh what is actually in the store and type it here. The app shows the difference against its own figure — that gap is real feeding above or below your plan, and it tells you whether your plan needs adjusting.
Simple purchase flow: Date → Feed → Quantity → Rate → Payment → Supplier → Save. Use ＋ Add new feed… inside the Feed dropdown when needed.

New Feed Purchase

one entry updates stock, Cash/Bank and supplier payable
DateFeedQty Rate/kgTotal SupplierPaymentCash / BankAllocationComment
Save once only: quantity enters Feed Stock immediately. Paid amount goes to the selected Cash/Bank account; unpaid balance goes to Supplier Payables. Daily feeding reduces stock automatically. Do not enter the same payment again in Accounting.
Recipe = what is inside the mix. Choose 50 kg, 100 kg or another batch size. Ingredient prices come from Feed Stock / purchase costing — do not type the same price twice.

Recipe Builder — Milking

Feed Master & Prices

ingredients come from here; purchase history updates costing
Feeding Plan = how much each animal group eats per day. Keep recipe ingredients in Recipes; here you only set finished mix, green fodder, dry/direct feeds and quantities.

Green fodder cost

cost the land, not the kilos
You cannot weigh fresh-cut fodder — so don't try. Enter each green-fodder cost once, including the actual payment date and how many months it should cover. Cash Flow records the full payment on the paid date, while P&L spreads it across the allocation months. Nothing is charged twice.

Group Feeding Plan

who gets how much per goat per day
One row per group — set what one goat in that group eats per day, and the cost works itself out. Press Recipe to change what goes into that group's mix.
Mix kg — concentrate you buy; priced from that group's recipe.
Green kg — an estimate, not a price. It does two jobs: tells you how much to cut each day, and splits the fodder-land cost fairly (a doe on 2 kg carries four times what a kid on 0.5 kg does).
Dry kg — toori/bhoosa you buy; priced per kg.
Fodder Rs/day — that group's share of the land cost, worked out for you.
Medicine and vaccines are not planned here — you buy them as needed, so they are recorded as real purchases on the Vaccines tab or as a Running cost. A month with none costs nothing.
GroupGoats Mix kg/goatGreen kg (share) Dry kg Fodder Rs/day Rs/goat/dayCost / month
e.g. "Show goats", "High-yield milkers" — then move animals into it from Herd → Move to
Adjusting rations: type straight into any box — the cost, buying list and stock all follow immediately. A rough starting point for Beetal-type goats, to change against your own vet's advice and what the animals actually clear up:
Kids — very little concentrate, mostly milk and soft green · Milking — the heaviest ration; feed to yield · Pregnant — moderate, then increase in the last 6 weeks (more again for twins) · Dry — the leanest; mostly fodder to hold condition · Bucks — moderate, lift before the breeding season · For sale — push concentrate to finish them.
Feed refused in the trough means the ration is too high; hungry animals and falling milk mean it is too low.

CAPITAL & OPERATIONS

CAPEX & OPEX

One accounting view separating long-term farm investment from day-to-day operating cost.

Accounting treatment: OPEX is included in operating P&L. CAPEX is excluded from operating P&L and is shown as project/fixed-asset investment. Both can reduce cash when paid. This view reads the existing Finance and Projects records — it does not create a second transaction.

Profit & loss statement

This is a working statement from your own records, not audited accounts. Owner funding is deliberately left out — it is money you put in, not money the farm earned. Salaries and fixed costs are counted at today's rates for every month in the period, from the date your books start (set on the Cash flow tab) — so older months are an estimate, not what you actually paid then.

Transportation & Logistics Report

shipment quantities, routes and delivery cost per unit
LOGISTICS
Each shipment automatically calculates delivery cost per litre, kilogram or item. The transport amount is recorded once as a Finance operating expense; when a payment account is selected it is also recorded as the matching Bank/Cash outflow, without creating a second P&L expense.

CAPEX & OPEX Report

CAPEX / OPEX
OPEX is included in operating P&L. CAPEX is excluded from normal operating P&L and tracked as project/fixed-asset investment. Cash figures below use actual paid movements, so this report does not create or duplicate transactions.

Projects & Capital Assets Report

CAPEX
Capital project spending is shown separately from operating P&L. Uncapitalized project spending remains Construction / Projects in Progress (CIP). When a project is completed and converted, that value moves from CIP to the fixed asset register without creating another cash payment or expense.

How it stays easy: you set each vaccine's rule once — either by age (e.g. kids at 30 days) or repeat (e.g. PPR every 12 months, for a whole group).
